title: College Algebra
description: A coherent College Algebra pathway from numerical and algebraic foundations through functions, equations, matrices, and discrete models; Weeks 13–15 are reserved for synthesis, cumulative review, and assessment.
outcomes: Simplify algebraic expressions and solve linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational, radical, exponential, and logarithmic equations while checking domain restrictions and extraneous candidates.
Construct and interpret linear, quadratic, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic models, connecting algebraic parameters to intercepts, rates, extrema, growth, and decay.
Analyze functions using notation, domain, average rates of change, arithmetic combinations, composition, and inverses, and justify conclusions with precise algebraic reasoning.
Represent and solve systems of linear equations with elimination and matrix methods, and interpret individual matrix entries and determinants in context.
Use graphical features and algebraic structure together to analyze zeros, factors, asymptotic restrictions, inequalities, and solution uniqueness without relying solely on numerical experimentation.
Evaluate arithmetic and geometric sequences and series, apply recursive definitions, and use the binomial theorem to determine specified terms and coefficients.

units.title: Real Numbers and Algebraic Foundations
units.summary: Build fluency with order of operations, signed numbers, rational arithmetic, exponent rules, scientific notation, and equivalent algebraic expressions. Emphasize that parentheses and exponent scope matter, that canceling means dividing by a common nonzero factor, and that simplifying should preserve the original expression's value and restrictions.
objectives: Evaluate numerical expressions involving integers, fractions, powers, and scientific notation using correct operation order.
Simplify polynomial expressions by distributing, combining like terms, and factoring out a greatest common factor.
Apply exponent laws to products, quotients, and powers while attending to nonzero denominators.

units.title: Linear and Absolute-Value Equations and Inequalities
units.summary: Solve linear equations by inverse operations and justify each transformation as an equivalence. Develop interval and integer reasoning for linear and absolute-value inequalities, reversing inequality signs when multiplying or dividing by a negative; interpret |x-a| as distance and distinguish equation solutions from inequality solution sets.
objectives: Solve linear equations containing parentheses and fractions and report exact solutions.
Solve absolute-value equations by analyzing the two distance cases and combining all solutions.
Interpret linear and absolute-value inequalities to determine integer solutions and boundary behavior.

units.title: Coordinates, Lines, and Linear Modeling
units.summary: Connect ordered pairs and the coordinate plane to slope, intercepts, and equations of lines. Move among point-slope, slope-intercept, and graphical information, then use constant-rate models in applications; keep slope as vertical change divided by horizontal change and verify that proposed points satisfy both equations at an intersection.
objectives: Calculate slope and intercepts from coordinate pairs and linear equations.
Determine coordinates associated with lines and intersections by solving appropriate linear equations.
Build and interpret a linear model from a fixed amount and a constant unit rate.

units.title: Functions, Domain, Rates, Composition, and Inverses
units.summary: Treat a function as a single-valued input-output rule and connect notation to evaluation, tables, and graphs. Determine real domains before simplifying standard expressions, compute average rates using change in output over change in input, and distinguish (f+g)(x), f(g(x)), and inverse notation; an inverse reverses inputs and outputs rather than producing a reciprocal.
objectives: Evaluate functions and average rates of change from explicit formulas over specified intervals.
Determine real domains and simplify arithmetic combinations of functions.
Compute compositions and inverse-function values by interpreting input-output order.

units.title: Quadratic Equations and Models
units.summary: Solve quadratics by factoring, taking square roots, completing the square, and using the quadratic formula, selecting a method that fits the structure. Interpret roots, vertex coordinates, and the discriminant in graphs and models; include every real root, retain exact radicals when requested, and check that applied answers respect time and other contextual restrictions.
objectives: Solve quadratic equations over the real numbers by factoring, square roots, and the quadratic formula.
Use the discriminant and vertex formula to determine root structure and optimize quadratic models.
Translate projectile or revenue relationships into quadratic equations and interpret admissible solutions.

units.title: Polynomial Functions and Division
units.summary: Analyze polynomial degree, leading terms, zeros, factors, multiplicities, and possible turning points as connected features of one function. Use grouping and long or synthetic division to rewrite polynomials, and apply the Remainder Theorem for efficient evaluation; remember that a squared factor repeats a zero, while x squared plus a positive constant contributes no real zero.
objectives: Expand and factor polynomial expressions using structure and grouping.
Divide polynomials and use the Remainder Theorem to connect quotients, remainders, and function values.
Infer distinct real zeros and bounds on turning points from factored form and degree.

units.title: Rational Expressions, Equations, and Inequalities
units.summary: Simplify and combine rational expressions by factoring first, finding common denominators, and recording values excluded by the original denominators. Clear denominators only with those restrictions in mind, test all equation candidates, and solve rational inequalities with sign charts rather than cross-multiplying by an expression whose sign is unknown; open and closed endpoints require separate attention.
objectives: Simplify rational expressions and add rational expressions using factored common denominators.
Solve rational equations while rejecting candidates excluded by an original denominator.
Use sign analysis of rational inequalities to count specified integer solutions with correct endpoint treatment.

units.title: Radical Expressions and Power Equations
units.summary: Evaluate roots and rational exponents using the connection between radicals and powers, attending to even-root domains and principal-root signs. Isolate radicals before raising both sides to a power, then substitute every candidate into the original equation because squaring can introduce extraneous solutions; for even powers, include both real signs when both satisfy the original equation.
objectives: Evaluate numerical expressions involving square roots, cube roots, and rational exponents.
Solve equations containing isolated radicals and verify candidates in the original equation.
Solve rational-exponent and integer-power equations with correct domain and sign decisions.

units.title: Exponential Functions and Equations
units.summary: Interpret f(x)=ab^x through its initial value and constant multiplicative factor, contrasting exponential growth with linear addition. Solve same-base equations by equating exponents and other bases with logarithms, and apply growth, compound-interest, and half-life models; distinguish the exponent's time unit from the number of compounding or decay periods.
objectives: Evaluate exponential functions and solve exponential equations using common bases and logarithms.
Interpret initial values, growth factors, compound periods, and half-lives in exponential models.
Report exact exponential-equation solutions and contextually appropriate numerical model values.

units.title: Logarithms and Applications
units.summary: Define logarithms as inverses of exponential functions and use that definition to evaluate and solve rather than memorizing isolated rules. Apply product, quotient, power, and change-of-base relationships only when logarithm arguments are positive; after solving logarithmic equations, enforce the original domain, and interpret logarithmic scales such as pH and seismic intensity as exponent-based comparisons.
objectives: Evaluate logarithmic expressions using inverse-exponent and logarithm properties.
Solve logarithmic equations and reject any candidate outside the original arguments' domains.
Interpret pH and seismic-intensity models using common logarithms and powers of ten.

units.title: Systems of Equations and Matrices
units.summary: Solve two- and three-variable linear systems by substitution and elimination, interpreting a unique solution as simultaneous satisfaction of every equation. Organize coefficients in matrices, use matrix multiplication entry by entry, connect a nonzero two-by-two determinant to invertibility, and distinguish the position of an entry from its numerical value.
objectives: Solve two-variable and three-variable linear systems and identify a requested coordinate.
Compute two-by-two determinants and entries of inverse matrices.
Multiply compatible matrices by combining rows and columns to determine individual entries.

units.title: Sequences, Series, and Binomial Reasoning

objectives: Find specified terms of arithmetic, geometric, and recursively defined sequences.
Evaluate finite arithmetic sums and convergent infinite geometric series using appropriate formulas.
Use the binomial theorem and combinatorial coefficients to determine a specified expansion coefficient.
